previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of COPD and recurrent pneumonias, was admitted for shortness of breath, cough, and low-grade fever. Imaging showed bibasilar opacities consistent with atelectasis rather than new pneumonia. She was treated for a COPD exacerbation with a five-day course of prednisone, levofloxacin, and nebulized bronchodilators. Her symptoms improved during the two-day stay, though she remained on 2L oxygen at discharge. Chronic conditions including hypothyroidism, anxiety, and chronic pain were managed with continued home medications. A one-week supply of oxycodone and methadone was provided due to a missed pain management appointment. She was discharged home with service to follow up with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with COPD, h/o recurrent pneumonias, presents with 
respiratory distress, hypoxia, hypotension, and altered mental 
status in setting of likely RLL pneumonia  
.  
# Respiratory distress - differential includes pneumonia vs 
bronchitis/bronchospasm. Rapid improvement after nebs in the 
emergency room would be more consistent with the latter.  
Patient initially admitted to ICU given hypotension.  Was 
transiently on a norepinephrine drip, but was quickly weaned 
off.  Received IV vanc, ceftriaxone, and levofloxacin in the ICU 
but was transitioned to just PO levafloxacin on call out to the 
floor.  Patient tested negative for Legionella.  Anxiety also 
likely played a large part in her shortness of breath as she 
went up in her O2 requirement every time she became anxious on 
this admission.  Patient was discharged to complete a 7 day 
course of oral levofloxacin and a fast prednisone taper.  
Patient will continue on her home regimen of inhalers.
.  
# Altered mental status - resolved following nebulizers, likely 
secondary to hypoxemia/hypercarbia from respiratory distress
.  
# Hypotension - required norepi drip while in the ICU, but 
quickly weaned off.  Patient was discharged to complete a 7 day 
course of levofloxacin.
.  
# Chronic pain - patient was continued on methadone, oxycodone, 
and pregabalin per home regimen
.  
# Hypothyroidism - patient continued on levothyroxine  
.  
# Chronic gastritis - patient continued on omeprazole
.  
# Anxiety - patient continued on citalopram and klonopin
.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Chest, single AP semi-erect portable view.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ female with history of altered mental
status and decreased oxygen saturation.

___.

FINDINGS:  Single AP, semi-erect portable view of the chest was obtained. 
There is increased right base opacity and blunting of the right costophrenic
angle which may be a combination of effusion and right lower lobe
consolidation.  Patchy left base opacity may reflect atelectasis.  The cardiac
silhouette is enlarged and somewhat globular in shape which could be due to
cardiomyopathy or pericardial effusion.  There is no overt pulmonary edema. 
The aorta is tortuous.  Chronic deformity of the right mid-to-lower chest wall
in part due to multiple prior rib fractures is again noted.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Increased right base opacity with blunting of the right costophrenic angle
may represent a combination of pleural fluid and right lower lobe pneumonia. 
Patchy lateral left lung opacity may reflect atelectasis.  2. Persistently
enlarged cardiac silhouette could be due to cardiomyopathy and/or pericardial
effusion.

EXAM:  Chest single portable AP view.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  A ___ female with history of new right IJ
central venous line.

___ at 17:31.

FINDINGS:  Single and AP upright portable view of the chest was obtained. 
There is interval placement of a right internal jugular central venous line
with distal tip in the region of the proximal-to-mid SVC.  While external
artifact overlies the bilateral lung apices, no definite pneumothorax is seen.
Persistent right base opacity is seen concerning for pneumonia with possible
small right pleural effusion.  Otherwise, there has been no significant
interval change since the prior study one day earlier.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Shortness of breath, community-acquired pneumonia.  Followup.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, there is no relevant
change.  The right more than left parenchymal opacities show unchanged extent
and severity.  Unchanged size of the cardiac silhouette, no evidence of newly
occurred focal parenchymal opacities.  Unchanged course of the right central
venous access line.  Unchanged appearance of the bilateral rib fractures.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
>25 PMNs and >10 epithelial cells/100X field.  Gram stain indicates extensive contamination with upper respiratory secretions. Bacterial culture results are invalid.  PLEASE SUBMIT ANOTHER SPECIMEN.
